statement: Tolerance is one full unit in the last decimal place to which depths in that file are written. Where depths use mixed precisions, use the finest precision seen.
application: Each written depth is allowed one full unit of its own last decimal place. A depth written at the finest precision in the file is held to that finest unit and is not given a coarser allowance. A coarser spelling is held to its own last place, so rounding a finer grid onto fewer written digits stays inside the unit that was written.
source: Derived by rounding analysis, consistent with the domain expert's rule that differences must be checked for rounding error. Not a number he gave. Each written depth is judged at its own last decimal place. STRT carries up to half a unit of rounding and each depth up to half a unit independently, so the worst-case combined error is one full unit. Awaiting expert review of the full-unit rule and the per-depth precision rule.
